messages.subject: Side-by-side strip plots
parts:
Hi:

Inspired by Prof. Bryan Hanson's example the other day, I became curious as to how to dodge strip plots correctly in ggplot2.

# Manufactured data:

d <- data.frame(A = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 10)),
                B = factor(rep(rep(c(1, 2), each = 5), 3)),
                y = as.vector(mapply(rnorm, 5, c(5, 7, 10, 5, 12, 14))) )

I am looking to get strip plots for each level of factor A dodged by the levels of factor B, but my simplistic efforts have been in vain thus far.

# The initial basic plot:
g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = a, y = y, color = b, fill = b))
g + geom_point()

None of the following work wrt the desired outcome:

g + geom_point(position = 'dodge')           # Nothing changes
g + geom_point(position = 'dodge', width = 0.4)     # Ditto, but I expected this...
g + geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5))    # Not quite...

The same message appears at each invocation, associated with the position = argument:
ymax not defined: adjusting position using y instead

The last attempt makes some progress in the sense that the B groups align on either side of the A level, but the values are jittered rather than in a vertical strip.

The message confuses me in that I'm trying to adjust the x-position of the strip plots  :)  Moreover, the help page says that the arguments are width and height.

I've consulted the book and the archives of this group but haven't found out how to produce such a graph.

So the question is: how to get pairs of strip plots at each level of factor A?

TIA,
Dennis

parts: Glad to be of inspiration!  I never was able to get my problem solved in the original way I was thinking, but ended up using the a table geom in ggExtras to good effect (see attached).  Ran your code, and I see what you are after Dennis, but I’ve got no insights as to a solution.  Still a lot to learn here.... Bryan
